s: Welcome to Word Kitchen, the podcast where we learn English words together.
Our five words are wallet, receipt, price, change, and cash.
Let us start with the word wallet.
A wallet is a small flat case.
You keep your money and cards in a wallet.
My wallet holds my cards, my money, and even a photo of my cat.
I check my wallet every morning before work.
But last year I lost my wallet at the supermarket.
I went back to the shop, and a worker found my wallet.
He gave it back to me.
So remember: always keep your wallet in a safe place.
A receipt is a small paper.
It shows what you paid for.
When you buy something, the shop gives you a receipt.
It is proof that you paid.
Last week I bought a jacket.
The receipt was in the bag.
I kept the receipt because maybe the jacket is too small.
If you want to return something, you need the receipt.
That is the rule in many shops.
And one more thing about a receipt.
Some shops send a receipt by email now.
A paper receipt or an email receipt, both are good.
The price is the money you must pay for something.
Before I buy, I always look at the price.
If the price is too high, I wait for a sale.
Yesterday I saw shoes with a high price.
That price was too much for me.
In my street, the price of bread went up last month.
The price tells you if something is cheap or expensive.
So always check the price first.
A good price makes shopping fun.
Change is the money you get back after you pay.
At the end of the day, I put all my change in a box.
My box of change is full.
Last week I counted my change.
You should count your change too.
Cash is money in coins and paper notes.
Not a card, just real cash.
Do you use cash or a card?
For small shops, I pay with cash.
You see it, you spend it.
If you lose cash, it is gone.
A card can be stopped, but cash is cash.
I keep a little cash in my wallet for emergencies.
The price tells you the cost.
And cash is real money in your hand.
Let us make a small story.
Yesterday I went to the market with my wallet.
And I kept the receipt in my wallet.
When you get change at a busy shop, count it fast.
And keep the receipt until you are sure about the thing you bought.
A receipt in your wallet is safe.
Money words are simple but powerful.
Practice these words when you shop this week.
Thank you for listening to Word Kitchen.
